pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

updates.content:
$OTC is the token I’m paying the most attention to on Solana, aside from $STONK.

The dev launched it on Pump, making it the second-earliest platform to launch on Solana. Within just one month, through its buyback and desk mechanism, more than 32% of the token supply has been burned, while the platform has accumulated nearly $700M in trading volume.

Today alone, trading volume has exceeded $40M. For OTC tokens, 50% of creator revenue is used for buybacks and burns, while the other 50% goes toward desk dividends. The dev takes no fees. I think this is a very genuine flywheel mechanism.

For other tokens launched on the OTC platform, 70% of the revenue is distributed to holders, 10% is used to buy back and burn $OTC, 10% goes to the desk, and 5% is distributed to OTC holders, while the developer only receives 5% of the protocol fees. On top of that, the dev is actively working on adding more features and creating additional revenue streams.

A team that has received this much support from the community is still struggling to move up because a small number of holders are selling heavily. I don’t believe this situation will last forever. Once those tokens are fully sold and the buybacks accumulate enough, I believe $OTC could see a massive move upward.

I believe in this, just like I believed in $STONK when I bought it at $0.029 and eventually made more than a 10x return, earning over $100K. Based on its development on Pump, I believe $OTC could reach a market cap of $20M–$50M.

I posted this information in Chinese yesterday when the market cap was around $3.5M, but not many people saw it. So I’m translating it into English and reposting it.

The current total supply is only 679M, with a true FDV of less than $6M.

If you believe in it, join me in waiting for a new ATH.

Good luck to us all!

comment.comment:
Spent a couple hours pulling OTC's actual on-chain data instead of
reading the chart, and a few things genuinely surprised me.

Start with supply. The mint started at 1B. Current supply is
695,711,307. That means 304,288,693 OTC — 30.43% of the entire
supply — is already gone. Burned. Not locked, not vested, not
"scheduled." Gone. Mint authority is null, freeze authority is null,
metadata is immutable, and there's zero transfer tax. Nobody can
print more, freeze your wallet, or change the rules. RugCheck gives
it a 1 with an empty risk array.

Then there's the part most people miss: this thing actually earns.
Protocol revenue to date is 27,339 SOL, about $3.18M. Of that,
18,654 SOL — $2.17M, or 68.2% — has been paid out to holders.
371,735 individual payouts. 3.9M wallet-level payments. 17,869
wallets still receiving right now, across 305 different assets.
Sit with that for a second: the protocol has distributed roughly
66% of its entire current market cap back to holders. Last
distribution went out minutes ago, not last week.

And the buyback isn't a promise, it's a receipt. Budget allocated
was 1,503 SOL. Actual spend is 1,711 SOL — they've overspent the
buyback budget by 208 SOL out of pocket. 2,715 separate burn
transactions. Holding balance is exactly 0, meaning every single
token bought gets burned immediately rather than sitting in a
treasury someone could dump. Last 24h alone burned 507,860 OTC,
up from 233,291 the day before. The burns literally never stopped.

Market's at $3.27M. Buy/sell ratio over 24h is 20,061 to 7,132 —
almost 3 to 1 — while price is down 24%. That's not distribution.
That's accumulation into weakness.

47,225 holders. 24,979 coins launched on the platform, 21,602 still
earning. Verified team account. LP locked.

I'm not going to tell you what to do. I'm just saying the burn
wallet doesn't care how you feel about the candle.
